Description

Noxious stimuli and inflammatory mediators open TRPV1 and ATP-gated P2X3 and P2X2/3 channels on the nerve endings in the joint, which lets sodium and calcium in and potassium out. The resulting depolarisation opens voltage-gated sodium channels, NaV1.8 among them, and the nerve fires action potentials towards the spinal cord. Blocking TRPV1, NaV1.8 or P2X3 reduces joint afferent firing and pain behaviour in osteoarthritis models.
